chapter: Chicago, Lee Collins and the road
title: Playing white house parties with trumpeter Lawrence Tocca
summary: Danny and Tocca played a few tunes repeatedly at house and lawn parties for white riverfront crowds.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: All right. So I'm playing. This is New Orleans. And there's all kinds of things going on. And you
begin to play for White folks. You play house parties. You play lawn parties. You play on the riverboats.

There were millions of house parties. You play the ....(?).... There was a woman in ...(?)., a White woman who used to give parties. And me and Lawrence Tocca(?), we played a series of parties for her.
Well, I don't know this White woman's name.
But you said Lawrence Tocca(?). Who was Lawrence Tocca(?).

Lawrence Tocca(?) was a trumpet player. This was one of the first little(?) bands. We had about six numbers we would do, and we'd play them repeat... The people didn't know. A lot of them was drunks, and it was Blacks, so they... As long as you had a Black Jazz band, you was doing something. "Them Colored boys," or whatever, they could play. So if you knew six tunes, it was all right.

So we played the parties, and that's when I began to see how people are like, you know. They had all these fast... They weren't out-and-out whores, but they were fast women, good-time women. Or maybe they weren't. And they had all these guys from the riverfront with the money, acting like... I saw them like gutbucket White folks. And they was drinkin' hard and talkin' loud, signifying.
